$meta.name: Construct visual tokens
$meta.summary: Reconciled visual primitives for the Moderne CLI. Colors are semantic (never decorative). Typography has four roles. Glyphs are paired with color to reinforce meaning. Every token traces back to evidence in audit/ or context/. Behavioral / API tokens are deliberately absent.
$meta.scope: Visual layer only. No exit codes, output contracts, or framework heuristics. See reconciliation.md for the per-token derivation and gaps.md Part B for what is intentionally not tokenized here.

evidence_keys.audit: audit/cli-inventory.md surface IDs (e.g. ERR-002, BAN-002), and audit/cli-deltas.md / cli-categorized.md references.
evidence_keys.context: context/cli-help-text-rewrites.pdf (Annie Rimbach), context/error-states-ui-uplift.pdf (Jayd Jackson), context/cli-help-text-journey-map.partial.html (CSS color tokens are authoritative).

color.$description: Semantic color tokens. Every color encodes a meaning; no token is decorative. Source values come from the journey-map CSS terminal classes (.t-cyan, .t-green, etc.). Single yellow token is shared across six expressions per D-03; disambiguation is by glyph + leading word + position, not by additional color.

page.role: Outer page background in mockups. Not emitted by the CLI itself; used in design surfaces only.

terminal.role: Terminal frame background. Emitted by the host terminal, not by the CLI; documented so design mockups can match the rendering target.

panel.role: Box / chrome border in mockups. Not emitted by the CLI.

primary.role: Section headers, banners, default emphasis. Bold weight where used.
applies_to: Section headers (USAGE / WHAT WENT WRONG / TRY / FLAGS / EXAMPLES)
Close banners (MOD SUCCEEDED / MOD FAILED / MOD PARTIALLY SUCCEEDED — color overrides for state)
evidence: audit BAN-001 / BAN-002 / BAN-003 / BAN-004 / BAN-005

body.role: Default reading text. Body of error WHAT WENT WRONG, body of help-text prose, success and partial-success body lines.
applies_to: EXAMPLES body lines (excluding the leading $ prompt)

supporting.role: Glosses, descriptions, paragraph prose under section headers, placeholder values inside cyan commands, child lines beneath onboarding steps.
applies_to: └ child lines under numbered onboarding steps
Descriptions in NEXT STEP / WHAT TO DO NEXT bullets after the em-dash
evidence: context/cli-help-text-rewrites.pdf — top-level mod onboarding, mod config -h descriptions

metadata.role: Demoted / footer / gutter content. Used to recede content the user should see but not focus on.
applies_to: Demoted support line in error TRY block (D-10) when other suggestions are present
Demoted deprecated flags in help text (J)
TECHNICAL DETAILS section (D-09 extrapolation) — when stack trace appears in user-facing template
evidence: context/error-states-ui-uplift.pdf — Jayd's demoted 'Still stuck? Report to support@moderne.io' line

info.name: cyan
info.role: Runnable commands, inline command references, hyperlinks, [incubating] tag. Cyan signals 'this is interactive content the user can type or click'.
applies_to: Inline command references in prose (replaces bold per D-12)
Hyperlinked content (OSC-8 wrapped — log paths, support email, dashboard URLs, repo paths, data-table paths) per Q
Numbered onboarding step commands (1–9 in Annie's top-level mod)
evidence: audit D-12 (inline references), audit D-15 (hyperlinks), audit category Q

success.name: green
success.role: Success state. Used on the close banner and on inline ✓ glyphs only — never on body text or commands.
applies_to: MOD SUCCEEDED WITH WARNINGS — text after the warning marker is body color, but the SUCCEEDED token can render in green where the framework distinguishes the two states
Numbered step indices (1–9) in onboarding ladder

danger.name: red
danger.role: Error / failure. Used on the failure preface, the close banner phrase, the ● bullet on error sections (WHAT WENT WRONG, TRY), and on the inline ! Error: marker.
applies_to: MOD FAILED close banner (BAN-004 failure variant)
● bullet on WHAT WENT WRONG and TRY section headers
! Error: inline marker in compact / usage error tier
✗ row glyph in tables when status is failure

warning.name: yellow
warning.role: Single yellow token covering six expressions per D-03. Disambiguation is by glyph + leading word + position, not by color subdivision.
applies_to: PARTIAL SUCCESS: preface (BAN-004 partial variant) + MOD PARTIALLY SUCCEEDED close phrase
evidence: context/error-states-ui-uplift.pdf — Jayd's mod search frame (⚠ + ? Hint + recovery)
context/cli-help-text-rewrites.pdf — Annie's ? Hint and ! Note inline tags
audit D-03, WARN-001, BAN-003, BAN-004, BAN-005

fallback.$description: Color fallbacks per S. Cascade is 24-bit truecolor → xterm-256 → no color. NO_COLOR=1 honored. Glyph + leading word + position must carry semantic when color is absent — every codified pattern must read in NO_COLOR + ASCII-only mode.
fallback.truecolor: Use the hex values above directly (24-bit ANSI escape).
fallback.xterm_256: Approximate to the nearest xterm-256 index. (Indices are framework-determined; visual system does not pin them.)
fallback.no_color: Emit no color escapes. Glyph + leading word + position carry the semantic. Banner phrases (MOD SUCCEEDED / MOD FAILED) remain bold; sectionizer characters (●, ▶, ✓, ⚠, ?, !) print as ASCII fallbacks per the glyph table.

typography.$description: Four typography roles, distinguishable by weight + color. Section headers use slight letter-spacing (0.02em in mockups) to differentiate ALL-CAPS from inline emphasis.

section_header.letter_spacing: 0.02em (mockup-only; terminals don't render letter-spacing — the casing carries the visual delta)
section_header.color: color.text.primary (or color.semantic.danger when prefixed by ● in error sections — the bullet is colored, the header text remains primary white)
section_header.supersedes: picocli's bold + underlined section headers (HELP-001). Underline is dropped per category I.

primary.role: Default reading text. Body of WHAT WENT WRONG, body of help-text consequence prose, success and partial-success body lines, the body of EXAMPLES (excluding the leading $ prompt).

supporting.role: Glosses, descriptions, child lines, placeholders inside cyan commands, gloss text after em-dash in NEXT STEP / WHAT TO DO NEXT bullets, empty-state lines.
evidence: context/cli-help-text-rewrites.pdf — └ child lines and section descriptions
context/error-states-ui-uplift.pdf — gloss text in TRY bullets

metadata.role: Demoted / footer / gutter. Receded content. Used for the demoted support line, deprecated flag listings, $ prompt prefix, and the optional TECHNICAL DETAILS section.

monospace.$description: All in-terminal output is rendered in the terminal's configured monospace font. Mockup chrome (outside the .terminal frame in the journey map) uses the .mono fallback stack: SF Mono, Fira Code, Menlo, Consolas, monospace.

spacing.$description: Single hierarchy. Resolves D-20's 2/4/8-space drift. Vertical rhythm comes from blank lines between sections (always exactly one).

section_content.role: Indentation of body content under a section header (USAGE, FLAGS, WHAT WENT WRONG, TRY).

list_item_continuation.role: Indentation of sub-items within an enumerated/bulleted list inside a section. Used for the inlined command line beneath a ▶ recovery action verb, and for example continuation lines.
evidence: context/error-states-ui-uplift.pdf — ▶ recovery action + indented command on the next line

retired.note: Used by FactoryOutput today (D-20). Retired in the visual system.

between_sections.role: Between the close of one section's content and the next section header.

header_to_content.role: A section header is followed immediately by its first content line — no blank line between.

around_close_banner.role: Close banners (MOD SUCCEEDED / MOD FAILED / MOD PARTIALLY SUCCEEDED / MOD SUCCEEDED WITH WARNINGS) get exactly one blank line above them. F-08 documents an asymmetry on the failure path; the visual system codifies symmetry.

around_failure_preface.role: FAILURE: preface line is followed by one blank line before the first ● section.

glyph.$description: Glyphs are paired with color tokens (color.semantic.*). Every glyph has an ASCII fallback (S). Glyph + color + leading word + position together discriminate semantically — no token relies on color alone.

section_marker.color_default: Inherits the section's semantic — color.semantic.danger for error sections (WHAT WENT WRONG, TRY); color.text.primary for neutral action headers (● Loading recipe, ● Searching 47 repositories).
section_marker.role: Major section / action header marker. Always paired with a section header phrase or an action verb.
evidence: audit ACT-001, ERR-002 (● Where, ● Try, etc.)

actionable_bullet.color_default: color.semantic.info (cyan) when the bullet leads a command. Bullet inherits color.text.metadata when the entire row is demoted (e.g. the support line under D-10).
actionable_bullet.role: Actionable bullet. Always paired with an imperative verb or a runnable command. Used in error TRY block, in success WHAT TO DO NEXT block, and in NEXT STEP help blocks.
actionable_bullet.supersedes: The legacy '> ' next-step bullet (D-04). The '> ' shape is retired in favor of '▶'.

success_marker.color_default: color.semantic.success (green) on the glyph; body text in color.text.body.
success_marker.role: Sub-task success indicator. Used on a single line summarizing what was done (e.g. ✓ 42 repositories modified).
evidence: context/error-states-ui-uplift.pdf — ✓ in mod run sub-task summary

warning_marker.color_default: color.semantic.warning (yellow) on the glyph; body text in color.text.body.
warning_marker.role: Inline warning indicator. Used to lead a line that conveys a non-fatal warning state (⚠ 0 repositories searched — all 47 skipped).

hint_marker.color_default: color.semantic.warning (yellow) on the glyph + the leading word 'Hint:'.
hint_marker.role: Inline hint. Used to surface anticipated questions or to acknowledge ambiguity inside a section. Always paired with the leading word 'Hint:'.
hint_marker.disambiguation: Same '?' character is used for prompts (O); position + cursor presence + leading-word disambiguates (a hint says 'Hint:' immediately after; a prompt has no 'Hint:' and presents an input cursor).
evidence: context/error-states-ui-uplift.pdf — ? Hint: in WHAT WENT WRONG block

note_marker.color_default: color.semantic.warning (yellow) when leading word is 'Note:'. color.semantic.danger (red) when leading word is 'Error:' (compact / usage error tier per D-02).
note_marker.role: Inline note or inline error marker. The leading word ('Note:' vs 'Error:') and the color disambiguate severity.

child_connector.role: Sub-description line beneath a numbered onboarding step. Single use in the artifacts (top-level mod onboarding ladder).

shell_prompt.role: Leads each example command in the EXAMPLES block. Visually present, semantically just a typographic convention to mark 'this is a runnable command'.

diff_failure.role: Per-row failure marker in tables (when a tabular surface tracks per-row success/failure). Extrapolated — the artifacts do not show a CLI-output table with row status.
evidence: Extrapolated from audit category P (table primitive) and the existing _NO_COLOR cross glyph used in some per-site renderers

banner.$description: Layout-level structural elements. Two start-banner variants (UTF-8 box-drawing and ASCII fallback per D-22) and four close-banner variants (success, partial, success-with-warnings, failure).

start.shape: Logo + version, centered, no color. Two layouts.
start.ascii_fallback: @-art logo (current BAN-001 fallback for non-UTF-8 terminals).

link.$description: Hyperlink rendering rules per Q. Cyan text via color.semantic.info; underline is left to the terminal's link-rendering preference.
link.transport: OSC-8 escape sequences (existing AdvancedLinks.A / link helpers).
link.underline_policy: The CLI does not impose an underline. Terminals that render OSC-8 links with their own underline are honored; terminals that don't are not compensated for (no fallback bracket form).

linkable_targets.repository_paths: linked (new — D-15 flagged the gap; visual system promotes them)
linkable_targets.recipe_ids: linked when a public recipe page exists for the tenant; otherwise plain cyan

link.fallback: When OSC-8 is not supported (terminal capability), emit plain cyan text without escape codes. No bracket / parenthesis fallback.

machine_readable.$description: Visual fallback rules for --csv / --json / --streaming modes per R / D-14.
machine_readable.out_of_scope: Whether errors should be wrapped in a structured envelope (JSON {error, suggestions[]}) and whether errors stream to stderr vs stdout — both behavioral, see gaps.md Part B.
